survivingClaim: PROVED (author and referee): dual-feasible points of the Legendre LP restrict along divisibility chains; alpha log x <= 8 + o(1); every limit point of dual-feasible points is feasible at every real scale, has density 0, psi(t) <= 3 log2 t + 3, and a Dirichlet transform holomorphic in Re s > 0; at density 1 the sawtooth discrepancy is >= (1/8 - o(1)) log x for integer-supported b. MEASURED (1e4..1e7): v log x/x falls from 4.08 to 2.86 with +-0.2 fluctuations, limit undecided; the optimum vanishes at fixed t; the optimum at qx restricted to x has objective -0.39 to -0.52 sqrt x at q = 2, 3 against +1.0 sqrt x. No statement about zeros.
obstruction: The cofinal limit of dual-feasible points keeps none of nu_1(x) ~ sqrt x: integer unit steps against Y log Y force any bounded-discrepancy cofinal dual to density 0, and the LP optima live at t ~ x in x-dependent Moebius-resonant configurations that are not sections of one measure. A fixed cofinal b is controlled only in mean square (MV-CAP); the pointwise bound is the open Moebius sum sum_k mu(k) r_b(x/k) (the source's Step 7).
controlsThatDefeat: E_a = zeta(s+a)zeta(s-a): passes every step (chain returns exponent 1/2 + a; nothing separates it from zeta at the level of exponents; ARGUED)
Beurling: Lambda_a >= 0 holds, power-size sawtooth discrepancy
DH, Liouville sign twist, theta^3: fail only at Lambda_a >= 0 (the separating step is positivity with log discrepancy)
lesson: Do not re-run limits of optimal Legendre duals. The only open item is the pointwise sum of mu(k) r_b(x/k) for one fixed r_b.
refereeNote: All PROVED steps re-derived. Measured range corrected: v log x/x reaches 2.864 at x = 1e7, below the first stated range; size law mu(m) sqrt(m)/sigma(m) only approximate.

newNodes.statement: Every limit point of Legendre-LP dual-feasible points is feasible at every real scale and has density 0, psi(t) <= 3 log2 t + 3.
Feasibility of a Legendre-LP dual point at qx implies feasibility of its restriction at x.
Pointwise polylog bound for sum_k mu(k) r_b(x/k) for one fixed cofinal r_b.
